sources.title: Jennifer Birch: Current Research on the Historical Development of Northern Iroquoian Societies
sources.note: Direct author-uploaded scholarly article, 2015, Tionontaté section. Sites south of Georgian Bay appear after circa 1580; contrasting Humber Valley and Neutralia origin proposals, pottery connections. Does not identify 1492 polygon as established confederacy.

sources.title: Charles Garrad: Paired Villages, Continuity and Variability among the Petun
sources.note: Direct Arch Notes 16(1), January/February 2011, pages 5 onward. Paired-village interpretation, Wolf/Deer groupings, larger/smaller settlements; specific historical village identifications remain proposals.

sources.title: Charles Garrad: The Petun and the Beaver
sources.note: Full indexed primary research paper, 2003. Page4 beaver-bone frequencies, page8 smaller villages and Odawa visitors interpreted. Direct open fails; indexed original gives full relevant pages. Avoid turning bone proportions into dietary calories or ethnicity tests.

sources.title: Samuel de Champlain: The Voyages and Explorations, volume2
sources.note: Full indexed institutional primary historical text, printed page99, January 1616 visit, maize and feast gifts of meat and fish. English translation of French account; do not repeat outdated editorial claims about identity.

sources.title: Charles Garrad: The Plater-Fleming BdHb-2 Site, a Review
sources.note: Full indexed original Arch Notes89(3), pages7 to25. Kettle/pottery comparison, metal goods and red tubular bead assemblage. Direct fetch challenge. Small bead sample explicitly not a census or exact independent date.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Single imported record1492 to1500, decoded world_1492 bbox[-80.7686,43.6732,-79.5086,44.6326], south Georgian Bay. Public opening warns early date predates securely documented historic villages. Do not share Huron card or absorb modern Wyandotte records; narrative distinguishes separate early polity and later mixed descendant identity. Modern writing witness explicitly2022, not ancient Petun. /aboutus/our-culture/ duplicates substantial older official history page used by huron; cumulative attribution checked separately.
